Hi all — quick recommended plan based on Acme's traffic profile (p50/p95 token sizes and 400 QPS peak). I kept estimates conservative; happy to iterate after we see the sample traces.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Continuous batching: Configure small, latency-aware batches with an upper token-delay cap (~10ms) to keep p95 low while getting batching benefits. Expect ~30-45% throughput improvement over no-batching for this request mix; tail latency increase ~+10-25ms depending on model and token distribution.

- Streaming + batching: Use streaming-first path where partial token flushes are sent when the batch reaches the cap or after a short token time window (~10ms). This preserves perceived latency while allowing batching gains. Note: streaming increases implementation complexity for KV cache alignment but is supported.

- Prefix/KV caching: Cache common prompt prefixes and retrieval results per-tenant (not per-user) to maximize hit rate while keeping memory bounded. For your 3% long-session tail, keep a separate large-KV pool. Expected cost savings: 15-30% token compute reduction if retrieval + prompt prefixes are highly repetitive.

- Quantization: Recommend testing 4-bit quantized variants for the 13B-class models and int8 for larger 35B+ models. Typical throughput improvements: 1.5–2.5x and memory reduction ~2–4x. Latency impact depends on kernel selection; in our infra you should expect slight p95 improvements due to reduced memory pressure.

- Model variants: Start with a quantized 13B variant for canary (quality vs cost sweet spot). Keep 35B/70B as a higher-quality fallback behind smart routing. We can route requests by SLA tier or confidence score. Estimated unit cost delta: 13B quantized ~base, 35B quantized ~2.5–3x, 70B ~4–6x.

- Autoscaling & dedicated pools: For predictable latency, reserve a small dedicated pool for peak hours and allow burst capacity on shared clusters. Dedicated pools reduce variability at a committed cost.

- Canary & eval plan: Run canary with 5k real-sample requests comparing 13B quantized vs current model using our eval harness; track ROUGE/answer-accuracy and embed-based similarity. Gate rollout on regression <2% on quality metrics and p95 latency within target.

Next steps:
1) I'll produce a short cost/latency table for the proposed configs (continuous batching windows, cache hit assumptions, and model variants) by tomorrow.
2) Marissa — can you confirm when Acme will drop the 2k sessions and whether we should also collect traces with streaming enabled?

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk the table together.
